---
title: "Comparing Total MEs across models"
subtitle: "Example 5.2.e of Mize and Han (2025), in R: mediation/attenuation"
---

Does the total effect of a college degree on self-rated health shrink once
family income is in the model? Fit the model without income and the model
with it, and combine them with [`suest`](/software/suest_r/index.qmd) to test
the difference in the Total ME. The same example in Stata is on the
[`totalme` page](/software/totalme/examples/across-models.qmd).

## Load and prepare the data

::: {.r-run}
```r
library(haven)           # Read Stata data
library(marginaleffects) # Marginal effects and hypotheses
library(nnet)            # Multinomial logit
library(suest)           # Combine models

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tdmize/Rfunctions/main/ME_helper_functions.R")

gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss.dta")
gss <- gss[gss$year >= 2000 & gss$year <= 2021, ]

vars <- c("healthR", "college", "race4", "age", "woman", "parent", "married", "faminc")
gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss[vars]), vars]

fvars <- c("healthR", "college", "race4", "woman", "parent", "married")
gss[fvars] <- lapply(gss[fvars], as_factor)
nrow(gss)
```
```{.r-output}
[1] 19292
```
:::

## Fit and combine the models

```r
basemod <- multinom(healthR ~ college + race4 + age + woman + parent +
  married, data = gss, trace = FALSE)
medmod <- multinom(healthR ~ college + race4 + age + woman + parent +
  married + faminc, data = gss, trace = FALSE)

fit <- suest(basemod, medmod, model_names = c("Base", "Income"))
```

## Total ME in each model

`totalme()` returns the Total ME in each model:

::: {.r-run}
```r
tme <- avg_comparisons(fit,
  variables = list(college = "reference"),
  newdata = gss,
  hypothesis = totalme(fit))
tme
```
```{.r-output}
  Group Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 Base      0.159    0.00605 26.3   <0.001 505.4 0.147  0.171
 Income    0.118    0.00673 17.5   <0.001 225.7 0.105  0.131

Term: college
Type: response
```
:::

## Test the difference

::: {.r-run}
```r
hypotheses(tme, hypothesis = difference ~ revpairwise)
```
```{.r-output}
        Hypothesis Estimate Std. Error  z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 (Base) - (Income)   0.0414    0.00276 15   <0.001 166.6 0.036 0.0468
```
:::

The difference is the part of the total college effect that family income
accounts for, with its standard error.
